source_span: China absorbed ~25% of the 20mb/d that transited the Strait; remove that shock absorber and GIR says fair value is roughly $10-15 higher... the risk premium — can still be considerably higher than we are pricing today
source_chain: Mideast export disruptions (Hormuz closure, pipeline damage, refinery attacks) are only partly offset by dark-fleet rerouting and China's reduced demand, therefore Goldman's own fair-value math implies crude is UNDER-pricing the supply risk (GIR: fair value $10-15 higher if China's Hormuz shock-absorption stops; Struyven: +$20/bbl per 10% sustained Mideast export cut; Dortmans: the risk premium 'can still be considerably higher than we are pricing today'), therefore the tail risk is a further spike toward $125+, not a reversion lower. Invalidation: a durable resolution of the physical Mideast supply disruptions themselves (not a diplomacy headline) — the note explicitly frames a ceasefire/de-escalation as its own separate risk to the desk's *long* oil position, not as the event that legitimately erases the premium.
pulse_chain: Brent's $16 premium over 'JPMorgan's $90 fair value' already prices in 4 million b/d of supply losses beyond the 10 million already gone, therefore a diplomacy headline (Thursday's Trump-Xi meeting, per JPMorgan) reprices that $16 away entirely, therefore crude falls toward fair value while the physically real diesel/refined-product shortage persists and keeps the Fed's hiking cycle alive. No invalidation for the premium-compression leg; the Trump-Xi meeting is presented as the event that 'takes the $16 out of crude for good.'
why: The chain is inverted and misattributed: no JPMorgan note in the corpus makes this $90-fair-value/ceasefire argument, and the one bank (Goldman, via GIR/Struyven/Dortmans in this file) that actually argues fair-value math for crude concludes the premium is under-priced and could go considerably higher on further Mideast disruption, the opposite of the pulse's claim that the premium is inflated and set to bleed out on a diplomacy headline.
